ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be performed against (i) the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's restricted and politically exposed person indicators under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information; (ii) UN Security Council sanctions lists as implemented under the Prohibition of Financing of Offenses to Public Interest Act; (iii) the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (iv) the EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists for cross-border payment flows; and (v) the FATF high-risk jurisdictions call-to-action list. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any person acting as nominee shareholder, holding ten percent or more equity, or exercising significant influence over automated dropshipping payment rails. Screening must be automated, continuous, occasioned by every transaction, and must include fuzzy matching, phonetic transliteration matching between Korean and romanized scripts, and adverse media review of all shareholders, directors, and beneficial owners. All screening decisions must be documented and made available for regulatory production to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit upon demand.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (I-ROOS) operated by the Supreme Court of Korea (www.iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory name clearance under the Korean Commercial Act requires a registered company name to be written in Korean characters. The name must consist of (1) a distinctive business name, (2) the legal form suffix Yuhan Hoesa, (3) an objective business purpose, and (4) a registered office city identifier where necessary. Romanized and foreign-script names are not independently registrable; an official phonetic transliteration may be registered as a secondary name and must follow the Revised Romanization of Korean system. The registry performs a four-tier comparison: exact Hangul match, phonetic Hangul match, Hanja variant match, and English/romanized transliteration match. A proposed name that is not clearly distinguishable from existing names in the same registry will be rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must obtain the written refusal grounds from the registry officer through the I-ROOS portal, then file an administrative appeal with the Competent Administrative Appeals Commission under the Administrative Appeals Act within 30 days of notification. Alternatively, judicial review may be sought through revocation litigation before the Administrative Court under the Administrative Litigation Act. The filing must include the proposed name, proof of the clearance attempt, legal arguments distinguishing the rejected name from earlier registered names, and a fallback transliteration. Legal counsel should simultaneously request expedited review because the name clearance window and the registration timeline are interdependent.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is legally acceptable at the initial court registration stage if a utility address is supplied, but the National Tax Service will normally reject a virtual office for a value-added tax operator and e-commerce business because the operator must maintain a place of business capable of inspecting books, stock, and machinery under Article 5 of the Value-Added Tax Act. Banks, including merchant acquirers for automated dropshipping, generally require an actual commercial lease agreement and a site inspection before opening a corporate account. Therefore, a virtual office is not operationally sustainable for this medium-risk entity; it creates a strong indicator of shell status and will trigger enhanced due diligence or account closure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: business registration certificate, commercial lease agreement, proof of domestic inventory or contractual warehousing arrangement, employer payroll records, accounting records, VAT invoice posting status, and bank statements. Quantified risk: for a newly formed automated dropshipping Yuhan Hoesa with a medium-risk profile, unannounced site visits by the National Tax Service or a local tax office occur in roughly 30 to 40 percent of cases within the first 12 months, especially where turnover is volatile and payment flows pass through Stripe or PayPal without a local clearing account. Unannounced registry-based address verification visits by municipal authorities are rare, below 5 percent, unless consumer complaints or tax discrepancies are filed.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Sangbeop), Articles 287 through 294 (formation of a limited liability company), Article 287-2 (articles of incorporation), Article 287-3 (subscription of shares), Article 287-4 (payment of shares), Article 287-5 (registration of incorporation), and Article 289 (directors and auditors).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Korean Commercial Registration Office (Court Registration Office) under the Supreme Court of Korea, or the online portal 'Startup' (www.startup.go.kr) for electronic filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation (Deung-gi) and Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan), filed with the Commercial Registration Office of the local district court having jurisdiction over the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) under the Commercial Act. However, the entire subscribed capital must be fully paid in cash at the time of incorporation, and the funds must be deposited into a bank account in the company's name. The bank's certificate of deposit must be submitted with the registration application. There is no escrow account requirement beyond this initial deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (Yuhan Hoesa) 

WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea on [date], and the Board of Directors is authorized to take all necessary actions to effectuate the Company's operations and governance; 

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that: 

1. Share Capital Subscription: The Board ratifies and confirms the subscription of the entire issued share capital of the Company, consisting of [total number] shares of no par value, each fully paid in cash, as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation. The Board acknowledges that the total paid-in capital of [amount] KRW has been deposited into the Company's designated bank account, and the bank's certificate of deposit is attached hereto as Exhibit A. 

2. Banking Authorization: The Board authorizes the opening of a corporate bank account with [Bank Name] and designates the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer as the sole authorized signatories for all banking transactions, with dual signatures required for any transaction exceeding [threshold] KRW. The Board further authorizes the execution of any banking agreements, the issuance of corporate credit cards, and the establishment of online banking credentials. 

3. Registered Office: The Board adopts the registered office of the Company at [full address], as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and appoints the Chief Executive Officer to execute any lease, service, or utility agreements necessary for the establishment and maintenance of such office. 

4. Statutory Officer Appointments: The Board appoints [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Company Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until their successors are duly elected and qualified. The Company Secretary is authorized to file all statutory returns, maintain the corporate records, and ensure compliance with the Commercial Act. 

5. General Authorization: The Board authorizes any officer to execute all documents and take all actions necessary to achieve the foregoing resolutions, and any actions taken prior to this resolution in furtherance of the Company's formation are hereby ratified and approved. 

This resolution is effective as of the date of its adoption and shall be recorded in the minutes of this meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Articles of Incorporation Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Commercial Registration Office (Court Registration Office) or online via the Supreme Court's Registration Information Center (IRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator must first reserve the company name with the Commercial Registration Office to ensure uniqueness. The name must include 'Yuhan Hoesa' or its English equivalent. After name approval, the Articles of Incorporation must be drafted in Korean, containing the company name, purpose, registered office address, total authorized shares, and the names of initial shareholders. The articles must be notarized by a notary public. The notarization fee is approximately KRW 40,000. The articles must be signed by all incorporators. The notarized articles are a prerequisite for the subsequent capital deposit and registration steps.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, the applicant may file a new name application with a revised name. If the articles are rejected for non-compliance, the applicant must amend the articles and re-notarize them, incurring additional notary fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in Korea (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must open a temporary corporate bank account in the company's name and deposit the full subscribed capital. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit (capital deposit certificate) confirming the amount and the account holder. This certificate is a mandatory document for the registration application. The deposit must be made before the registration filing. The bank may require the notarized articles and identification of the incorporators. The certificate is valid for a limited period (usually 30 days) and must be submitted with the registration application.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the certificate due to incomplete documentation, the incorporators must rectify the missing documents and reapply. If the deposit is not made in full, the certificate will not be issued; the incorporators must complete the deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the local district court having jurisdiction over the registered office, or online via the IRO portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must file the application for incorporation registration with the Commercial Registration Office. The application must include the notarized articles, capital deposit certificate, and a statement of the registered office. The registration fee is calculated based on the capital amount (approximately 0.5% of capital, with a minimum of KRW 50,000). The application must be signed by all incorporators or their legal representatives. The registration office will review the documents for compliance with the Commercial Act. Upon approval, the company is officially registered and receives a Certificate of Incorporation. The registration must be completed within 2 weeks from the date of the capital deposit.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office (lease agreement or consent letter)
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is rejected due to deficiencies, the applicant will receive a notice specifying the issues. The applicant must correct the deficiencies and resubmit within the statutory period (usually 2 weeks). If the rejection is based on substantive non-compliance, the applicant may appeal to the court or file a new application after rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration: Business Registration and Tax Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and local tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation, the company must register for business tax purposes with the local tax office within 20 days. The company must obtain a Business Registration Certificate (Saeupja Deungrok) and a corporate tax identification number. The application must include the Certificate of Incorporation, the company's articles, and details of the business activities. The company must also register for value-added tax (VAT) if its annual revenue exceeds KRW 80 million. Additionally, the company must open a corporate bank account in its name and register for social insurance (National Pension, Health Insurance, Employment Insurance) for employees. The business registration is essential for issuing tax invoices and conducting commercial activities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the business registration is delayed or rejected, the company may face penalties. The company must ensure all documents are accurate and complete. If the tax office requests additional information, the company must provide it promptly. If the registration is denied, the company may appeal to the NTS or reapply after correcting the issues.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, accessed electronically via the Home Tax Service (HTS) portal at www.hometax.go.kr, with physical customs clearance and border cargo alerts handled by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity that creates a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) domestically first obtains corporate registration from the competent court registry office and then applies to the relevant local district tax office for Business Registration using the standard NTS application. The applicant must file the business registration form together with the articles of incorporation, proof of corporate registration, lease or address proof for the Korean place of business, identity and passport/corporate equivalent of the representative, and a power of attorney if a Korean tax representative is appointed. After acceptance, NTS issues the Business Registration Certificate containing the 10-digit business and VAT registration number, which serves as the corporate TIN. If the foreign non-resident entity has no domestic place of business but supplies electronic or digital services to Korean individual consumers, it must complete the special foreign business operator VAT registration through the Home Tax Service by submitting the foreign registration certificate, charter or equivalent constitutional document, certificate of tax residence from the foreign jurisdiction, statement of Korean consumer revenue, and a power of attorney to a resident tax agent. NTS then issues a foreign business operator registration number for VAT filing and withholding purposes. For entities that will physically clear goods through Korean customs, an additional importer/exporter code must be obtained through UNI-PASS before any export declaration or import clearance is accepted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean law does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election for Yuhan Hoesa corporations. All Yuhan Hoesa are separate legal entities taxed at the entity level under the Corporate Tax Act, and no hybrid mismatch pass-through election is available under Korean tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value Added Tax Act, together with customs duty and import VAT at the border for physical goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic corporations: registration is mandatory with no turnover threshold; any Yuhan Hoesa engaged in VAT-taxable business must register with NTS within 20 days of business commencement. Foreign non-resident electronic or digital service suppliers: mandatory registration is triggered when annual Korean consumer digital-service supplies exceed KRW 30 million; below that threshold, special foreign registration is not required unless the foreign entity opens a Korean place of business. Physical dropshipping imports into Korea are taxed at the border through customs import VAT regardless of supplier turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory for business-to-business supplies made by a registered Korean LLC. A Yuhan Hoesa must issue an electronic tax invoice using the NTS Home Tax Service or an approved certified ASP and transmit it to NTS no later than the day after the supply date. The electronic tax invoice must state the supplier registration number, recipient registration number, supply date, supply value, VAT amount, and transaction description. Korea does not operate a physical fiscal stamp or real-time cash-register clearance; instead, anti-fraud controls are based on mandatory electronic tax invoice interlocking, the Cash Receipt System, and automatic cross-matching of purchase, sales, banking, and customs declarations by NTS.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Korea qualify for zero rating under the Korean Value Added Tax Act when the goods have been shipped to a foreign buyer and the actual departure from Korea is evidenced by an accepted export customs declaration. Services supplied to non-residents may likewise be zero-rated when the service falls within the foreign-earned services or offshore digital service categories and is actually consumed outside Korea. In a direct dropshipping model where goods are sent from a third-country supplier directly to an overseas consumer without ever entering Korean customs territory, Korean export zero-rating is not applicable because the transaction lacks Korean indirect tax nexus; such a supply must be documented by commercial invoices, courier waybills, and bank settlement records from the source jurisdiction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Certificate) accepted through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system
Bill of Lading or multimodal transport document evidencing physical departure from Korea
Commercial invoice showing the overseas buyer and export terms
Packing list matching the export declaration and transport documents
Foreign exchange settlement certificate or inward remittance certificate proving receipt and repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If NTS or Korea Customs Service detects a false export declaration, forged transport documents, black-market exchange conversion, or failure to repatriate export proceeds within the required 180-day period, the zero-rated export is retroactively recharacterised as a taxable domestic supply. The taxpayer then becomes liable for the 10% VAT on the suppressed export value, interest under the National Tax Collection Act, additional penalty taxes of up to 20% for dishonest filing or up to 10% for underpayment, and possible criminal referral for customs fraud or foreign exchange violations. The burden of proof rests on the exporting entity, and substantiation documents are subject to post-clearance audit and demand notices in the course of VAT reassessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (The Bank of Korea) acting in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; operational reporting and monitoring are executed through the Foreign Exchange Information System operated by the Korea Federation of Banks and delegated authorized foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a managed but de facto functional convertibility regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is convertible for current-account trade and service-related cross-border payments, including digital content subscriptions, software licensing, logistics, and dropshipping inventory procurement, provided there is a valid underlying commercial contract, electronic trade declaration, and proper bank documentation. Capital-account transactions, however, are subject to a negative-list system: foreign direct investment, external borrowing, and foreign-currency loans require notification, registration, or approval through a designated foreign exchange bank or the Bank of Korea. There is no general statutory surrender obligation compelling conversion of export proceeds into Korean won when proceeds are lawfully retained in a foreign-currency account at an authorized domestic bank; nevertheless, export proceeds must be repatriated to South Korea within the prescribed statutory period and documented through the Foreign Exchange Information System. Profit remittance by a foreign shareholder is generally permissible after external audit, corporate tax settlement, and dividend board approval, but the remitting bank will require evidence of the foreign investment report, tax clearance, and the board resolution declaring dividends. In practice, banks treat cross-border digital dropshipping revenue with heightened scrutiny because of the absence of physical goods movement and the complex aggregation of payments through third-party payment service providers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds arising from dropshipping transactions must be received within 18 months from the date of the export declaration or electronic trade receipt, unless an extension is granted by the authorized foreign exchange bank for justified commercial reasons. There is no mandatory fixed conversion ratio to Korean won; exporters may retain foreign currency in an authorized foreign-currency account at a domestic bank. However, each receipt must be reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System, and any conversion into Korean won is executed at the prevailing market rate. For automated e-commerce platforms where sales are aggregated and settled through Stripe or PayPal, the consolidated foreign-currency settlement into a Korean bank account must be fully reconcilable to underlying order data, product descriptions, cross-border customer and logistics records, and, where applicable, customs clearance documentation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and linked Foreign-currency Account)
Capital Escrow Account for inward foreign investment and Foreign-currency Operational Account
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW) and Trade Settlement Account
Foreign Currency Account and Export Proceeds Receivable Account
Corporate Operating Account for SME treasury clearance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Foreign fintech Electronic Money Institutions and offshore digital payment platforms do not constitute authorized foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and cannot directly open Korean won settlement accounts or execute FX operations in South Korea. Such EMIs are legally barred from servicing a domestic corporate entity in a manner equivalent to a licensed bank. The entity may use global payment service providers such as Stripe and PayPal solely as customer collection tools, but all treasury concentration, conversion, and disbursement must ultimately occur through a domestic licensed commercial bank or a locally licensed financial services company with a bank-backed payment gateway partnership.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Domestic banking practice requires the statutory representative director, especially a foreign-resident director, to appear physically in branch for identity verification and final KYC interview when opening a new corporate account for a non-resident-owned Yuhan Hoesa. Remote consular proxy opening is not a standardized or generally accepted allowance under current internal compliance policies. A power of attorney may permit a Korean-resident officer to submit ancillary documents, but the final signatory interview and biometric identity verification must be completed by the accountable director or a delegated director physically present at the domestic branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained beneficial ownership layers and inadequate source-of-wealth evidence for non-resident shareholders of an automated dropshipping entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extract, full share register, international passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners, notarized source-of-funds declarations, personal and corporate bank statements covering the preceding 12 months, notarized deeds or investment agreements for initial capital contributions, and evidence of tax residence in the shareholder jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared automated dropshipping business model and aggregated PSP settlement flows from Stripe and PayPal, creating an elevated risk of layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed platform agreements between the entity and PSPs, complete merchant settlement statements, a line-item sub-ledger of orders, customer transaction logs with geolocation data, refund and chargeback policies, product source evidence, and a live read-only dashboard report reconciled to the bank account debits and credits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cross-border counterparty exposure and potential sanctions leakage due to an open-Internet customer base and global supplier network.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions screening reports covering the entity, suppliers, and customers; country exclusion and IP-geolocation blocking evidence; OFAC, EU, UN, and Korean Foreign Exchange Information System compliance policy; prohibited and restricted goods matrix; supplier due diligence files; and a negative news monitoring procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient substantive local presence in South Korea for an entity managed mainly by foreign shareholders with automated remote operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly registered local statutory director profile, resident registration and proof of address, lease agreement for the registered office or business address, payroll records and national pension and health insurance contribution evidence for any local employees, director engagement contract, board meeting minutes approving treasury mandates, and a documented business continuity plan.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign equity contributions should be routed by wire transfer to the entity's designated foreign currency account or capital escrow account at an authorized domestic commercial bank. The remittance instruction must carry the appropriate foreign exchange purpose code corresponding to direct investment, and the foreign investor must complete the foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before or within the statutory filing window. For foreign-currency loans from overseas shareholders, the loan agreement must be submitted to the authorized bank and registered under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act before UTILIZATION. Capital verification is evidenced by a bank-issued foreign currency receipt certificate, the certified capital increase registration, and reconciliation to the Korean corporate registry filing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier payments and logistics rails, SWIFT MT103 is used for direct telegraphic transfers of trade receivables and operational invoices; commercial letters of credit are preferred for high-value inventory purchases where documentary compliance protects both parties; documentary collections are acceptable for established suppliers under confirmed trade history. Every disbursement must be matched with the corresponding purchase order, import declaration or electronic trade record, and invoice. For cross-border service payments such as digital advertising, software licensing, and cloud infrastructure, the bank requires a service trade receipt, valid contract, and tax withholding certificate where applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Trade-backed forward foreign exchange contracts in Korean won for underlying export proceeds or import payables with proven documentary support
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currency exposures where physical settlement is restricted or prohibited
Cross-currency swaps limited to hedging identifiable foreign-currency liabilities and approved by the bank's internal treasury risk committee with real-exposure documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and 10% Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months from the fiscal year end; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, on or before March 31 of the following year; an extension of up to one extra month is available for book-closing reasons, and a further extension to June 30 may be approved by the district tax office if the company is subject to external audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or understating the tax base triggers a 20% unfaithful-return penalty, a 40% penalty for intentional misstatement, and an overdue-interest charge of 0.03% per day on unpaid tax; continued non-filing for more than one year can lead to a district tax office investigation, assessment based on estimated income, and administrative strike-off of the business registration for the e-commerce activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Semi-Annual Returns for Automated Dropshipping Supplies and Electronic Tax Invoice Data Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea via the Home Tax Service platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half year: submit by July 25 for the period January 1 through June 30. Second half year: submit by January 25 of the following year for the period July 1 through December 31. Electronic tax invoices issued to Korean counterparties must be transmitted to the NTS by the 10th day of the month following the supply date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or under-declared output VAT attracts a 10% negligent-discharge surcharge on the difference, plus 0.03% daily overdue interest on unpaid VAT; continued failure to file VAT returns for six months or more exposes the entity to a VAT investigation and business premises inspection, and continued non-filing for one year or more is an administrative forfeiture trigger for cancellation of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Preparation, Members Meeting Approval, and Corpus of Minute Book Records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office of the Yuhan Hoesa; no central government filing is required for a non-listed small LLC unless the external audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual members meeting must be convened and financial statements for the immediately preceding fiscal year must be approved within three months after the fiscal year end, meaning not later than March 31 for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Wilful absence of annual members meeting approval and unsigned financial statements is an irregularity under the Commercial Act; minority members can petition the court to appoint an auditor or order destruction of unlawful resolutions, and the entity can be subject to a court-ordered administrative liquidation if the company is unable to carry on business due to chronic statutory meeting failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent CPA External Audit Report Filing for Audit-Mandated Yuhan Hoesa Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service and the Securities and Futures Commission through the DART external audit report system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For companies crossing the statutory audit threshold, the auditor must be appointed within four months after the fiscal year end and the completed audit report must be filed with the Financial Supervisory Service within two weeks after the members meeting approval, with a final outer deadline of no later than April 30 following the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor, refusal to provide audit evidence, or failure to file the audit report can result in a criminal fine, a monetary penalty assessed by the Securities and Futures Commission, and disqualification of a director; if the company does not comply with the external audit order, the court may order dissolution in cases of public interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner Confirmation and Foreign Investor Change Notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Intelligence Unit of Korea through the registered agent and, for non-resident shareholders, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation of UBO records must be completed before the annual members meeting; any transfer of equity interest, change in registered capital contribution, or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing or false UBO declarations in the statutory registers expose the company to a penalty of up to KRW 50,000,000 under the financial transaction reporting rules and potential criminal sanctions for violation of the real-name financial transaction principle; continuing failure in a foreign-invested company case can cause cancellation of foreign-invested company preferences and forced divestment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A certified independent CPA audit is legally compulsory under the Korean Act on External Audit of Companies if the Yuhan Hoesa meets any of the following criteria: (a) total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000, which is approximately USD 9,000,000 at the current exchange reference level; (b) the company is a KOSPI-listed or KOSDAQ-listed company, or is a subsidiary or parent of such a listed company as defined in the Act; (c) the company is engaged in regulated financial, insurance, securities, electronic financial business, or any business requiring special audit under a separate statute; (d) the Securities and Futures Commission designates the company as an audit-designated company under Articles 9 through 11 of the Act because of a previous audit deficiency, overdue filing, or public-interest concern; (e) the company is a company with no registered CPA auditor within the required appointment window; or (f) the company is a large business group affiliate required by Presidential Decree to be subject to external auditor rotation and audit designation. There is no separate headcount or turnover threshold that alone creates a statutory audit requirement in the Republic of Korea for a private limited liability company; however, any e-commerce dropshipping entity that voluntarily prepares consolidated financial statements for public issuance or cross-border financing must obtain an external audit as a condition of the offering or financing agreement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: A listed or audit-designated Korean company must apply K-IFRS, which is the Korean adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards. A non-listed Yuhan Hoesa that becomes subject to external audit may apply the Korean General Purpose Financial Reporting Framework for Small and Medium Entities, commonly called SME K-GAAP, unless it voluntarily applies full K-IFRS. All corporate income tax base computations must start from accounting income determined under these approved standards and then apply the mandatory adjustments in the Korean Corporate Tax Act, including rules for inventory valuation, bad debt reserves, depreciation ceilings, and e-commerce transaction recognition. Automated dropshipping revenue is recognised as agency or principal revenue depending on the contractual relationship with the underlying supplier, and the entity must maintain point-of-sale, settlement, refund, and cross-border inventory records to support the accounting treatment.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a current ultimate beneficial owner register and perform a formal annual confirmation cycle before the members meeting, updating the name, nationality, residence, direct and indirect equity percentages, capital contribution amounts, dividend distribution rights, and voting control of every person ultimately owning or controlling the company. Any transfer of equity interest, admission of a new member, change of controlling person, or variation of capital contribution rights must be entered into the UBO register and reported to the corporate agent and the relevant Korean financial institution within 30 days of the change. For any non-resident member owning 10% or more of the entity, or any resident UBO using foreign payment settlement rails such as Stripe or PayPal, the change must also be made through the Foreign Investment Notification system with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or the competent dealing bank within the same 30-day window. Failure to complete the annual confirmation or to report a 30-day event is an administrative violation subject to Korean AML, FATF-aligned real-name financial transaction, and foreign investment reporting penalties.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 to USD 1,800 per annum for a professional registered office and corporate secretarial agent in Seoul or Sejong, including register custody, UBO confirmation assistance, notice handling, and compliance calendar monitoring
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 to USD 15,000 per annum for a Yuhan Hoesa within the mandatory audit threshold or undertaking a voluntary audit; fees may increase to USD 30,000 or more if the company engages in high-volume cross-border automated dropshipping with multiple payment rails, stock inventory, or consolidated reporting requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax top marginal rate plus 10% local corporate income tax surtax (2.4%), producing a 26.4% aggregate top marginal rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; progressive national rates are 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying high-tech foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones and Foreign Investment Zones may enjoy 100% corporate income tax exemption for the first five years and 50% reduction for the following two years under the Restriction of Foreign Investment Act; additional R&D tax credits up to 30-50% of qualifying R&D expenditure; reduction or exemption for income from new growth source technologies; patent-box-like 50% deduction of qualifying patent royalty income; tax deferrals for foreign direct investment capital expenditure are also available under certain statutory conditions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax return under Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act (Form No. 1 series and annexed tax reconciliation schedules), filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal (hometax.go.kr); transfer pricing schedules are attached where international related-party transactions exceed the statutory threshold
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; semi-annual interim corporate income tax prepayments are also required for corporations that paid tax in the immediately preceding tax year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate income tax return must be filed within three months after the end of each fiscal year under Article 60(1) of the Corporate Tax Act; if the financial statements are externally audited under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, the filing deadline may be extended by one additional month; payment of the self-assessed tax is due by the same statutory deadline

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification and tax period: Korean corporate registration number, entity legal name (Yuhan Hoesa), industry classification, ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110, business year commencement and closing dates, place of effective management, business address, and registered tax office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the foreign ownership percentage, country of tax residence of each non-resident shareholder, and passport or foreign business registration number; a Korean tax representative and domestic address for service must be identified; a missing domestic contact or foreign investment report under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act may result in rejection of the return and default assessment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement reconciliation pre-tax accounting income: gross dropshipping revenue, contra-revenue items, cost of goods sold, merchant network fees, payment processing charges, app development and platform subscription costs, freight and fulfillment expenses, and selling, general, and administrative expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Automated dropshipping revenue must be reported gross, not net of Stripe, PayPal, card, or bank fees; merchant processor chargebacks and refunds are separate deductible expense-line items; related-party platform fees and overseas warehouse fulfillment charges must be reported at arm's length and substantiated with contemporaneous documentation; underreporting platform revenue is the most common cause of NTS e-commerce audits

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax base reconciliation schedule: adjustments from book income to statutory taxable income, including non-deductible expenses, entertainment expense disallowance, fines, penalties, accrued but unpaid bonuses, donations, and non-deductible related-party payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident related parties that lack economic substance or exceed arm's length prices must be separately disclosed and adjusted in this schedule; the tax authority can import transfer pricing adjustments under Article 5 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs and the adjustment must be included in this reconciliation; non-resident directors' compensation is deductible only when at reasonable quantification and genuinely services are rendered for the Yuhan Hoesa

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation, amortization, intangible ownership, and inventory valuation: fixed assets, software and algorithm intangibles, patent and license amortization, dropshipping inventory at overseas fulfillment centers, and bad debt reserves
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Yuhan Hoesa has no owned warehouse and title passes solely through automated ordering, inventory may be minimal or zero; however, use of third-party fulfillment centers in the United States, Japan, or Europe creates foreign inventory and can create a permanent establishment or a foreign fixed base of operations; the corporate taxpayer must analyze whether functions performed through automated algorithms in Korea constitute core income-generating activities for treaty PE attribution and report foreign fixed assets accordingly

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward, tax credits, and non-resident investment incentives: net operating loss carryforward utilization, R&D credit, foreign direct investment credit, foreign tax credit, and the new growth source technology income reduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korea allows an NOL carryforward period of 10 years; a carryforward is disallowed if a foreign controlling shareholder or group fails the continuity of ownership test; a foreign tax credit is available for qualifying foreign-source dropshipping profits, but the credit is limited to the Korean corporate income tax attributable to the same foreign-source income; attach official foreign tax receipt and the NTS Foreign Tax Credit Schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International transaction and transfer pricing disclosures: intercompany sales, purchases, royalties, interest, management fees, payment processing services, algorithm licensing, and distribution transactions with foreign related parties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report every transaction with a foreign related party in the separate disclosure schedule; if aggregate intercompany transactions with foreign related parties reach KRW 50 billion or exceed other statutory documentation thresholds, attach the Local File and Master File; select and document the most appropriate arm's length method under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs; automated dropshipping platform fees should be tested under the Transactional Net Margin Method or Profit Split when the foreign related party contributes valuable intangible-driven functions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax on non-resident income: dividend distributions, interest, royalties, and other income paid or credited to non-residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold and remit the statutory 22% aggregate income tax and local income tax surcharge on gross dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-resident shareholders or counterparties unless a bilateral tax treaty reduces the rate; complete the withholding tax return in HomeTax and issue the statutory withholding certificate to the payee; a failure to withhold and remit makes the Yuhan Hoesa liable for collection and creates a non-deductible expense for the withholding amount

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident declaration, tax treaty relief, and beneficial ownership substantiation: tax residence certificates, beneficial ownership certificates, treaty article invocations, and reduced withholding rate applications
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For DTA relief, attach each non-resident beneficial owner's original Tax Residency Certificate, the statement confirming no pass-through or conduit arrangement, and the bank confirmation of ultimate beneficiary; for dividend shares, maintain the 24-month holding-period evidence where the DTA so requires; if the withholding agent applies the reduced treaty rate incorrectly, the Yuhan Hoesa risks a negligence penalty and the non-resident remains secondarily liable for the Korean tax shortfall

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, tax equalization, and CbCR information: reconciliation of worldwide taxable income, foreign-source taxable income, creditable foreign taxes, and country-by-country reporting flags
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only foreign taxes eligible under Korean law and paid on foreign-source income are creditable; an automated dropshipping entity with a foreign permanent establishment must file the foreign PE income reconciliation; where the Korean entity is part of a multinational group with consolidated revenue of at least KRW 1 trillion, attach the CbCR notification or indicate the reporting group member and jurisdiction; failure to report can trigger international information-reporting penalties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation, prepayments, credits, balance due, and payment confirmation: final taxable income, tax at progressive rates, local income tax surtax, interim prepayment offsets, tax credits, penalties, and net cash payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay any remaining tax by the filing deadline to avoid daily late-payment interest and negligence penalties; if the Yuhan Hoesa has no net Korean corporate tax due because of foreign tax credits, preserve the underlying source documents for seven years; a refund claim based on DTA reduced withholding or overpaid estimated taxes must be made in writing to the National Tax Service with the full documentary trail; a false declaration of zero taxable income for a non-resident-owned dropshipping entity is an immediate and auditable red flag

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and underreporting penalties apply under Article 47-3 of the Basic Act for National Taxes: 20% of the unpaid tax for underreporting, increased to 40% where the underreporting is fraudulent or intentional, plus a non-payment additional charge of 0.022% per day on delinquent tax; failure to submit transfer pricing documentation can trigger separate penalties under Article 12 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs; deliberate false corporate returns or false EDI filings constitute tax evasion under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, punishable by up to five years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 100 million, and where the evaded amount exceeds KRW 500 million the penalty escalates to three to ten years' imprisonment and a fine up to three times the tax evaded

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax on dividends paid by a Korean domestic corporation to a non-resident beneficial owner under Article 98(1) of the Income Tax Act, plus a 10% local income tax surcharge equal to 2% of the gross dividend, resulting in a 22% aggregate statutory withholding tax rate absent treaty reduction
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the foreign shareholder must obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate from the foreign tax authority, complete the Korean application for withholding tax exemption or reduction under the applicable tax treaty, submit a beneficial ownership declaration confirming the shareholder is not a conduit or letterbox entity, provide proof of shareholding period where the treaty requires a specified holding duration, and deliver the documentation to the Yuhan Hoesa as the Korean withholding agent before the dividend payment is executed; the withholding agent must report the treaty-reduced rate in the HomeTax withholding return; if tax was over-withheld, the non-resident may file a refund claim against the National Tax Service within the statutory five-year period, attaching the entire treaty package, payment confirmation, and beneficial owner chain; for treaty shopping, the National Tax Service applies the principal purpose test and may deny the DTA benefit where obtaining the treaty benefit is one of the principal purposes of the Yuhan Hoesa structure
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border interest and royalty payments to non-residents is 20% national income tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge, i.e. 22% aggregate; bilateral tax treaties commonly reduce these to 10% or 15% for interest and royalties, while pure business profits are not taxable in Korea absent a permanent establishment; Yuhan Hoesa must separately characterize payments for algorithm software, customer data, brand license, and platform integration as royalties or business-service fees, because the NTS strictly reclassifies disguised royalties as taxable royalty income and imposes the full 22% withholding, penalties, and daily interest on recharacterized amounts

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 50 billion aggregate cross-border related-party transaction amount in a fiscal year is the current statutory threshold under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs Enforcement Decree for mandatory simultaneous submission of the Local File and Master File; a Korean group member with prior-year revenue of KRW 100 billion or more and related-party international transactions at or above KRW 50 billion is also within the Master File obligation; group consolidated revenue of at least KRW 1 trillion triggers Country-by-Country Reporting notification; below the thresholds, taxpayers should still prepare contemporaneous TP documentation because the NTS may request it upon audit and absence of documentation shifts the burden of proof on the arm's length price
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply a Gulf Cooperation Council-style Economic Substance Regulations filing, but Korean tax law and BEPS minimum standards apply the economic substance doctrine through the substance-over-form rule, step-transaction doctrine, and Article 17 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs under which the tax authority may deny or recharacterize an unreasonable transaction or incorporation; for the automated dropshipping Yuhan Hoesa, Core Income-Generating Activities CIGA include the actual performance of order-matching algorithms, payment reconciliation, customer relationship intake, logistics control, and contracting decisions; if those activities are performed by the foreign non-resident parent and the Korean entity has no employees, no premises, no board authority, and no operating records, the Korean entity is effectively a shell and the NTS may reattribute taxable income to the real earner, applying severe penalties and treaty anti-abuse rules

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and economic substance failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Yuhan Hoesa is maintained as a Korean registration shell with no physical office, no employees, no substantive contracts, no Korean bank account with real decision-making authority, and no core income-generating activities performed in Korea; all automated dropshipping revenue is sourced through algorithms and foreign fulfillment contracts while Korean entity profits are stripped to foreign investors solely to access a favorable DTA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service is empowered under Article 17(1) of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs to disregard the artificial entity or recharacterize the transaction; a 20% negligence penalty applies for underreporting under Article 47-3(1) and a 40% penalty for fraudulent underreporting under Article 47-3(2) of the Basic Act for National Taxes; criminal prosecution for tax evasion under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act carries imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to KRW 100 million, aggravated to three to ten years and a fine of up to three times the tax evaded where the tax deficiency exceeds KRW 500 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may have the corporate veil pierced through fraudulent conveyance rules and the substance-over-form recharacterization, making personal assets available for collection of the Korean corporate tax liability; directors who knowingly authorized the shell structure can be named as joint and several collection targets, blacklisted as delinquent taxpayers, subjected to overseas travel restrictions, and prosecuted as co-principals in tax evasion or fraud; where the director prepares or falsifies corporate books, Article 8 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act imposes imprisonment up to three years or a fine of up to KRW 50 million

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Yuhan Hoesa files its corporate income tax return without preparing the Local File or Master File and without an arm's length analysis despite paying excessive foreign related-party charges for automated dropshipping platform access, payment processing, software licensing, customer data transfer, and management services; related-party charges are a flat 15% percentage of gross revenue with no comparability analysis, no functional risk policy, and no profit attribution study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS may make a transfer pricing adjustment under Article 2 and Article 5 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, increase taxable income, add a 20% negligence penalty under Article 47-3(1) of the Basic Act for National Taxes, and impose a 40% penalty for repeated or fraudulent international transaction mispricing; non-compliance with documentation standards permits the NTS to rely on its own estimate and deny burden-of-proof protections; criminal consequences can arise through false books and records under Article 8 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act with penalties of imprisonment up to three years or a fine of up to KRW 50 million, and where the transfer pricing adjustment is part of intentional evasion, Article 3 provides the aggravated imprisonment and fine regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or execute the false intercompany pricing may be personally liable to the extent they participated in causing the tax deficiency under Korean joint tort and company law creditor remedies; NTS collection authorities may seize personal bank accounts, vehicles, and real estate where assets were transferred out of the Yuhan Hoesa to shareholders; directors may be designated as delinquent high-value obligors and prohibited from overseas travel or denied foreign exchange conversions; criminal conviction can bar a director from service on Korean corporate boards and expose the director to extradition-assistance proceedings in treaty partner countries

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding tax evasion on profit repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Yuhan Hoesa repatriates profits to non-resident shareholders and foreign related parties through mislabeled 'service fees', 'data access fees', and 'management charges' without applying the statutory 22% withholding tax on constructive dividends, interest, or royalties, and without submitting the necessary tax residence certificate or beneficial ownership declaration to the Korean withholding agent; the true economic substance is a dividend distribution, and the non-resident investor enjoys a tax-free outflow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service recharacterizes the mislabeled payments as dividends or royalties under the substance-over-form rule and imposes the full 22% withholding tax, plus a 20% penalty for underwithholding under Article 47-3 of the Basic Act for National Taxes and daily delinquency interest at 0.022%; the failure to file withholding returns may be classified as an intentional concealment of tax under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, carrying imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to KRW 100 million, and up to ten years' imprisonment and a fine of three times the evaded tax when the amount exceeds KRW 500 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who participates in the disguised dividend scheme is personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax as a responsible withholding officer under Korean tax collection rules; civil asset restitution extends to personal bank transfers where the dividend was paid into directors' personal accounts; the director and the non-resident beneficial owner may be jointly blacklisted by the National Tax Service, and the Criminal Sentencing Committee may order seizure of director assets, travel bans, and imprisonment; in egregious cross-border cases, the director may face criminal extradition under treaty frameworks and personal directors' disqualification on grounds of breach of fiduciary duty and complicity in tax fraud
